tagline: A nighttime byway, four and a half miles under the lights.
intro: The byway starts at the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign, in the median just south of Russell Road, and runs north up Las Vegas Boulevard past Mandalay Bay, the southernmost resort, to the Sahara at Sahara Avenue, where the city limits begin. The Federal Highway Administration counts it among the country's only nighttime byways.

Before it was the Strip it was Highway 91, the Los Angeles Highway. Guy McAfee, a Los Angeles police officer and businessman, named it for the Sunset Strip back home. When the city tried to annex it in 1950, the casino men had the county make it two towns of its own instead.

moments.title: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
moments.text: Betty Willis designed it in 1959, with silver dollars spelling Welcome across the top. The north side, less photographed, reads Drive Carefully, Come Back Soon.

moments.title: Flamingo Las Vegas
moments.text: Bugsy Siegel took over and the cost went from $1 million to $6 million. The casino opened December 26, 1946. No resort on the Strip has run longer. Siegel lasted until June.

moments.title: Sahara
moments.text: The sixth resort on the Strip opened here in 1952 with an African theme. It anchors the north end, at the corner where the City of Las Vegas takes over.
